answer: An agent economy resists sybils by demanding a cost that cannot be cloned cheaply: verified work history, not a fresh address. Picture a harbour where every vessel must dock at a stone jetty before it trades, and that jetty logs each arrival publicly. A newcomer may emerge from any dune on the coast, but without a record of hauling real cargo it stays at anchor. Reputation accrues like opal forming in layers — slow, unmistakable, impossible to fake overnight. Empty clusters betray themselves by sharing one untested origin, while a proven trader carries a trail the network can check.
